questions.q: What does NULLIF(expr1, expr2) return when expr1 and expr2 are equal?
options: NULL
expr1, unchanged
expr2, unchanged
An error
questions.explain: When the two expressions are equal, NULLIF returns NULL instead of either value.

questions.q: What does NULLIF(expr1, expr2) return when expr1 and expr2 are NOT equal?
options: expr1, unchanged
NULL
expr2, unchanged
The larger of the two values
questions.explain: When the two expressions differ, NULLIF simply passes expr1 through unchanged.

questions.q: Why does LineTotal / NULLIF(OrderQty, 0) avoid a divide-by-zero error?
options: Dividing by NULL produces NULL instead of raising an error
NULLIF rounds OrderQty up to 1 whenever it's 0
NULLIF removes the row entirely from the result
SQL Server automatically skips any row where OrderQty is 0
questions.explain: NULLIF converts a 0 denominator to NULL, and division by NULL simply yields NULL instead of throwing a runtime error.

questions.q: What does COALESCE(LineTotal / NULLIF(OrderQty, 0), 0) do overall?
options: Guards the division from a zero denominator with NULLIF, then replaces any resulting NULL with 0 using COALESCE
Replaces LineTotal with 0 whenever OrderQty is NULL
Multiplies LineTotal by 0 whenever OrderQty is 0
Has no effect beyond the plain division
questions.explain: NULLIF prevents the runtime error, and COALESCE turns the resulting NULL into a clean 0 for display.

questions.q: How does NULLIF relate conceptually to COALESCE?
options: They solve opposite halves of the same problem — COALESCE turns NULL into a real value, NULLIF turns a matching real value into NULL
They are identical functions with different names
NULLIF is simply COALESCE with the arguments reversed
COALESCE only works on numbers, while NULLIF only works on strings
questions.explain: COALESCE recovers from a NULL by substituting a value; NULLIF protects against a specific value by substituting NULL for it.
